description: Synthetic public benchmark for contextual relevance in evolving domain intelligence.

cases.title: Changing engagement
cases.t0: A person regularly uses a specialized health information service and consistently engages with the information provided.
cases.t1: Interaction becomes less frequent and recent engagement is materially weaker than the earlier pattern.
cases.t2: The lower engagement persists across subsequent interactions.
cases.task: Determine whether the current interpretation of the person's relationship with the service should change and explain why.
cases.expected_property: Recent interaction evidence should be considered relevant to the current state rather than treating the earlier engagement pattern as permanently representative.
cases.failure_mode: Treat historical engagement as a stable user attribute.

cases.title: Intention versus behavior
cases.t0: A person states an intention to continue a health-related process.
cases.t1: Subsequent observed behavior diverges from the stated intention.
cases.t2: The divergence appears again in later interactions.
cases.task: Determine how the current interpretation should account for the difference between stated intention and subsequent behavior.
cases.expected_property: Later observed behavior should become relevant evidence about the current state while the earlier intention remains historical evidence.
cases.failure_mode: Treat an earlier stated intention as permanently authoritative.

cases.title: Changing circumstances
cases.t0: A person interacts with a specialized health information service under a stable set of surrounding circumstances.
cases.t1: A significant personal circumstance changes.
cases.t2: The person's subsequent interactions differ from the earlier pattern.
cases.task: Determine whether historical interaction evidence should retain the same current relevance.
cases.expected_property: A materially changed circumstance should trigger contextual re-evaluation rather than automatic continuity of the prior interpretation.
cases.failure_mode: Assume the same interaction pattern remains representative after a material contextual change.

cases.title: Trust trajectory
cases.t0: A person repeatedly relies on a specialized health information service.
cases.t1: The person begins questioning the service more frequently and reduces reliance on previous guidance.
cases.t2: The pattern continues across later interactions.
cases.task: Determine what the interaction trajectory says about the current relationship with the domain system.
cases.expected_property: Repeated changes in interaction can be treated as evidence that the current user-system relationship differs from its historical state.
cases.failure_mode: Treat trust as a fixed user property inferred from historical usage.

cases.title: New information changes relevance
cases.t0: A working interpretation is based on information available at an earlier point in time.
cases.t1: A later observation introduces information that materially qualifies the earlier interpretation.
cases.t2: The new information remains relevant in subsequent interactions.
cases.task: Determine how the later information should affect the current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: New evidence should be allowed to change the relevance or confidence of an earlier interpretation without rewriting what was known earlier.
cases.failure_mode: Preserve the earlier interpretation unchanged because it was previously reasonable.

cases.title: Irrelevant contextual change
cases.t0: A person's interaction with a specialized health information service is stable.
cases.t1: An unrelated contextual detail changes but has no demonstrated relationship to the interaction.
cases.t2: The person's behavior remains stable.
cases.task: Determine whether the earlier interpretation should materially change.
cases.expected_property: The system should resist changing its interpretation when the new information has no demonstrated relevance to the domain relationship.
cases.failure_mode: Change the interpretation merely because any new contextual information appeared.

cases.title: Matter posture change
cases.t0: A legal intelligence system evaluates a matter using information available at an earlier stage.
cases.t1: A later event materially changes the procedural or factual posture of the matter.
cases.t2: Subsequent information continues to reflect the changed posture.
cases.task: Determine whether the earlier interpretation should remain the dominant current reference.
cases.expected_property: The current interpretation should reflect the changed matter state rather than treating the earlier posture as permanent.
cases.failure_mode: Treat an earlier matter state as current after a material transition.

cases.title: Qualifying evidence
cases.t0: A working interpretation is supported by documents available at an earlier point in time.
cases.t1: A later document materially qualifies the earlier interpretation.
cases.t2: The later document remains part of the active matter record.
cases.task: Determine how the current interpretation should incorporate the later evidence.
cases.expected_property: The later evidence should change the relevance or confidence of the earlier interpretation when materially warranted.
cases.failure_mode: Preserve an earlier conclusion merely because it was established first.

cases.title: Changing objective
cases.t0: A person uses a legal intelligence system with one clearly stated objective.
cases.t1: The person's objective changes materially.
cases.t2: Subsequent questions and decisions align with the new objective.
cases.task: Determine whether the system should continue optimizing its interpretation around the original objective.
cases.expected_property: The current goal should become part of the relevant context while the previous goal remains historical.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the original objective as a persistent user attribute.

cases.title: Interaction trajectory
cases.t0: A user repeatedly engages with a legal intelligence system in a consistent pattern.
cases.t1: The user's interaction style, questions and follow-through change materially.
cases.t2: The new interaction pattern persists.
cases.task: Determine whether the current user-domain relationship should be interpreted as unchanged.
cases.expected_property: Persistent changes in interaction behavior should become relevant evidence about the current relationship with the domain.
cases.failure_mode: Treat interaction history as a static user profile.

cases.title: Historical record versus current state
cases.t0: A matter is understood using a set of historical facts and documents.
cases.t1: The matter evolves while the historical record remains unchanged.
cases.t2: The current matter contains materially different conditions from those present at the original assessment.
cases.task: Determine how historical evidence should relate to current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: Historical evidence should remain available but should be interpreted within the current temporal context.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the unchanged historical record as proof that the current state is unchanged.

cases.title: Irrelevant administrative change
cases.t0: A legal matter's substantive facts and objective remain stable.
cases.t1: An administrative detail changes without affecting the substantive matter.
cases.t2: The substantive state remains unchanged.
cases.task: Determine whether the substantive interpretation should materially change.
cases.expected_property: The system should preserve the prior interpretation when the new information does not materially affect the matter.
cases.failure_mode: Treat every change in metadata or administration as a substantive state transition.

cases.title: Changing personal constraints
cases.t0: A financial intelligence system evaluates a person using known circumstances and preferences.
cases.t1: Relevant personal constraints materially change.
cases.t2: Subsequent behavior reflects the new constraints.
cases.task: Determine whether the earlier user representation should remain the primary basis of current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: Current constraints should be treated as relevant to the present relationship with the financial domain.
cases.failure_mode: Treat an earlier personal profile as permanently representative.

cases.title: Changing objective
cases.t0: A person interacts with financial intelligence around a clearly stated objective.
cases.t1: The objective changes materially.
cases.t2: Later interactions consistently reflect the new objective.
cases.task: Determine whether the earlier objective should continue to dominate current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: The changed objective should alter current contextual interpretation while preserving the historical objective as part of the interaction history.
cases.failure_mode: Persist the old objective after the user has materially changed direction.

cases.title: Trust and continued use
cases.t0: A person regularly relies on a financial AI service.
cases.t1: The person's interaction frequency and willingness to rely on the service decline.
cases.t2: The decline persists across later interactions.
cases.task: Determine whether the current relationship with the service should be considered materially different from the historical pattern.
cases.expected_property: Interaction trajectory can become evidence about changing trust or engagement without treating those properties as fixed attributes.
cases.failure_mode: Assume historical usage guarantees continued trust or continued use.

cases.title: Behavior after interaction
cases.t0: A person receives information from a financial intelligence service and behaves consistently with their previous interaction pattern.
cases.t1: Subsequent interaction behavior changes after repeated experiences with the service.
cases.t2: The new pattern persists.
cases.task: Determine whether the interaction history itself has become relevant evidence about the current relationship with the system.
cases.expected_property: Later behavior should be interpreted as part of an evolving user-system relationship rather than as independent noise.
cases.failure_mode: Separate current behavior from the interaction history that preceded it.

cases.title: Historical evidence loses relevance
cases.t0: A financial intelligence system has a long history of observations about a user's behavior.
cases.t1: A sustained change in circumstances produces a materially different recent pattern.
cases.t2: Recent behavior continues to diverge from the older pattern.
cases.task: Determine how historical and recent evidence should relate to the current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: Historical evidence may remain informative while becoming less representative of current behavior after sustained change.
cases.failure_mode: Treat older observations as equally representative regardless of subsequent change.

cases.title: Irrelevant external information
cases.t0: A person's stated objective and observed interaction pattern remain stable.
cases.t1: An external information update occurs that has no demonstrated relevance to the person's objective or interaction.
cases.t2: The person's behavior remains unchanged.
cases.task: Determine whether the current interpretation of the person-domain relationship should materially change.
cases.expected_property: The system should preserve the previous interpretation when the new information has no demonstrated relevance to the current relationship.
cases.failure_mode: Overreact to contextual information without establishing its relevance.

cases.title: Operating conditions change
cases.t0: An operational intelligence system evaluates a fleet asset under a known operating context.
cases.t1: The operating context changes materially.
cases.t2: Subsequent observations continue under the new conditions.
cases.task: Determine whether the earlier assessment should remain the dominant current reference.
cases.expected_property: Current operating conditions should influence the present interpretation rather than assuming historical conditions still hold.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the earlier operating state as permanently representative.

cases.title: Operational history loses relevance
cases.t0: An operational system has a long history of observations under repeated conditions.
cases.t1: The operating environment changes and the recent pattern diverges from the historical pattern.
cases.t2: The divergence persists.
cases.task: Determine how historical observations should relate to the current operating state.
cases.expected_property: Historical regularity should remain evidence while becoming less representative when the underlying operating state changes materially.
cases.failure_mode: Treat historical operational regularity as a permanent characteristic.

cases.title: Action changes the next state
cases.t0: An operational decision is made using information available at the time.
cases.t1: The decision changes subsequent operating conditions.
cases.t2: New observations occur under the changed conditions.
cases.task: Determine how the later state should be interpreted in relation to the earlier decision.
cases.expected_property: The later state should be understood as occurring after a consequential action rather than as a continuation of the untouched earlier state.
cases.failure_mode: Interpret post-action observations as though the preceding action had no relationship to them.

cases.title: Operator behavior changes
cases.t0: A fleet system observes a stable pattern of interaction between an operator and an operational workflow.
cases.t1: The operator's behavior changes materially.
cases.t2: The new behavior persists across subsequent interactions.
cases.task: Determine whether the earlier behavioral pattern should remain the primary basis of current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: Persistent behavioral change should become relevant evidence about the current operating relationship.
cases.failure_mode: Treat historical operator behavior as a fixed characteristic.

cases.title: Context changes without domain change
cases.t0: The operational domain and its underlying purpose remain unchanged.
cases.t1: Relevant environmental or organizational conditions change materially.
cases.t2: The system continues operating in the same domain under different conditions.
cases.task: Determine whether domain continuity is sufficient to preserve the earlier interpretation.
cases.expected_property: Stable domain identity should be distinguished from changing operational context.
cases.failure_mode: Assume that an unchanged domain means the current state is unchanged.

cases.title: Irrelevant environmental change
cases.t0: An operational system is assessed under stable relevant conditions.
cases.t1: An environmental detail changes outside the system's relevant operating context.
cases.t2: Relevant observations remain unchanged.
cases.task: Determine whether the operational interpretation should materially change.
cases.expected_property: The system should avoid changing its interpretation when the environmental change has no demonstrated relevance to the operating state.
cases.failure_mode: Treat every environmental change as operationally material.
